scenes.heading: Why is the sky *blue*?
scenes.narration: Why is the sky blue? The answer is hiding inside sunlight.
Sunlight looks white. But it's really every color of the rainbow, traveling together.
Each color is a wave. Red waves are long and lazy. Blue waves are short and choppy.
When sunlight hits the air, tiny molecules bounce the short blue waves in every direction. The long red waves mostly pass straight through.

scenes.label: Blue scatters about *six times* more than red
scenes.narration: Blue scatters about six times more than red. So blue reaches your eyes from every part of the sky.
But here's the odd part. Violet scatters even more than blue. So why isn't the sky violet?

scenes.heading: Three reasons
items: The Sun sends out less violet
scenes.narration: The Sun sends out less of it. The upper atmosphere absorbs some. And our eyes are less sensitive to it.
At sunset, light crosses far more air. The blue gets scattered away, and red is what's left.
Blue sky by day. Red sky by evening. Same sunlight, different path.
